title: ExtH3
description: The ext-h3 extension, version 0.1 (proposed): where an entity sits on a globe, as an H3 cell and an integer-only transform in that cell's frame, beside the core transform a reader without the extension draws. Everything rides under the namespaced 'ext-h3' key: on entities (the placement) and on the environment (the package's frame: the cell whose centre is the local origin). The core schema leaves room for the key (unknown fields are allowed and must-ignored); this schema pins the extension's own shape. The H3 fields are authoritative and the core transform is derived from them by the producer (spec/extensions/h3.md, 'The one invariant'). Spec: spec/extensions/h3.md.

Cell.description: An H3 cell index, as H3's 15-digit lowercase hexadecimal string.

Resolution.description: The cell's H3 resolution, 0 to 15. Stated so a reader without an H3 library knows the translation unit; it MUST equal what the index encodes.

Body.description: The body the grid is laid on. 'earth' is the default and the only body this version defines a unit table for; a reader that does not know the body draws the core transform.

Frame.description: The environment's ext-h3 block: the package's local frame. Its origin is the cell's centre on the body's sphere; +X east, +Y up, +Z south; metres (the core's conventions).

Placement.description: An entity's ext-h3 block: its cell, and its transform relative to the cell's centre in the cell's own frame (+X east, +Y up, +Z south), as integers.

translation.description: Hundredths of the mean edge length of a cell at `resolution` (H3 4's getHexagonEdgeLengthAvgM: 0.584169 m at 15, so one unit is 5.84169 mm), along the cell frame's east, up and south.

rotation.description: Hundredths of a degree, intrinsic XYZ Euler like the core's rotation_degrees; each in -18000..=18000.

scale.description: Log2 fixed point per axis: round(log2(factor) * 1024). 0 is 1x, 1024 is 2x, -1024 is 0.5x.
